narrative.story: The annual calendar is Patek's own 1996 invention — a calendar that only needs correcting each March — and the 5396 of 2006 put it in the most restrained package the complication has had: twin day-month apertures under 12, analog date around the moonphase at 6, a 24-hour indicator, all in a 38.5mm case. White gold variants ran through dial generations (baton, Breguet numeral, blue sunburst) until the reference wound down in 2024.
narrative.collector_notes: Aperture alignment and crisp date-hand centering are the service tells. The 5396 trades well under the sports references, which makes it the value route into a complicated modern Patek.
